summary.plain: The first direct sighting of neutrinos bouncing gently off entire atomic nuclei rather than their individual parts, a process predicted 43 years earlier but never before caught, seen using a small caesium-iodide crystal at a US neutron facility.
summary.technical: First observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) at 6.7 sigma confidence, using a 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillator exposed to pion-decay-at-rest neutrinos from the SNS; characteristic energy/time signatures matched the Standard Model prediction, yielding improved constraints on non-standard neutrino-quark interactions.

title: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
why_it_matters: CEvNS had the largest predicted cross section of any low-energy neutrino interaction but had eluded direct detection for four decades because the nuclear recoils it produces are extremely small; its observation opened a new experimental handle on neutrino properties, supernova-neutrino detection, and dark-matter-detector background modeling, and enabled a new generation of compact neutrino detectors.
